results.summary:
Bumped actions/checkout and actions/setup-node from v4 to v7 at all 14 sites: the four workflows in .github/workflows, the two shipped templates in templates/actions, and the two test selectors that assert the pinned string. Major-tag pinning kept, matching the existing style and claude-code-action@v1; latest upstream re-checked with `git ls-remote` rather than trusted from the issue (checkout v7.0.1, setup-node v7.0.0).

The one migration note that touches us is caching. setup-node v5 turned automatic npm caching on by default and v6 narrowed it to "package.json names npm in packageManager or devEngines"; hkb has no dependencies and ships no lock file, and restoreCache throws "Dependencies lock file is not found" when there is none — a hard step failure. So every setup-node with a checkout behind it now sets `package-manager-cache: false`. It also matters for adopters: the shipped workflows only install hkb globally, so a cache would be saved and restored on every 15-minute tick for nothing, and setup-node's docs recommend disabling it in jobs with elevated privileges (release.yml's `id-token: write`, the kanban jobs' KB_TOKEN). release.yml's verify job is deliberately left without the flag — no checkout means no package.json to detect — and a comment there says so.

release.yml was not renamed and the npm publish step did not move. `registry-url` is unchanged across v4-v7 and stays unset in the publish job; the trusted-publishing assertion in test/release.test.js is intact, with only the version in the selector changed.

checkout's other majors are inert here. v6 moved the persisted credential to a separate file (input defaults unchanged, and v6.0.1 added worktree support for the includeIf it uses). v7 refuses to check out fork PR code from pull_request_target and workflow_run — kanban-dispatch.yml does have a workflow_run trigger, but it fires on the worker workflow, whose event is workflow_dispatch, and the step checks out the base repo's default branch with no `ref`, so the guard returns before it can throw.

docs/harnesses.md now names the self-hosted runner floor (v2.327.1) the Node 24 actions require — that is the one way this bump can break an adopter. Draft PR: #81.
